channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: Tajikistan Considers Withdrawing From the International Criminal Court
item.description: The lower house reviewed a draft resolution on 16 September; the trigger is the ICC warrant against Putin.

item.title: Israel's Elections Committee Bars All Arab Parties From the Knesset Vote
item.description: The decision, made before the 27 October election, must be approved by the High Court, which has overturned such bans before.

item.title: Pakistan Strikes 10 Sites Inside Afghanistan; At Least 4 Civilians Killed
item.description: After strikes hit Kandahar, Paktia and Khost provinces, cross-border gunfire continued along the frontier.

item.title: Iran Offers 7-Day Plan to Reopen Strait of Hormuz; Trump Rejects It
item.description: Iran's foreign minister set out the conditions; the US president rejected the proposal and said the naval blockade would stay.

item.title: ICT Week Uzbekistan 2026: 300+ Companies From 51 Countries Gather in Tashkent
item.description: The 22–25 September event focused on artificial intelligence, startups and the venture capital market.

item.title: Uzbekistan's state symbols: how the flag, emblem and anthem were adopted
item.description: How and when independent Uzbekistan's three state symbols were adopted: the State Flag on 18 November 1991; the State Emblem on 2 July 1992; the State Anthem on 10 December 1992. The meaning of each, what the colors and symbols stand for, and who created them. A facts-based, sourced history.

item.title: Russian Drone Hits 16-Storey Building in Central Kyiv: 14-Year-Old Killed
item.description: At least 7 people were injured in the 25 September morning strike; Ukraine's president said 282 drones were launched overnight.

item.title: What inflation is and why prices rise: a full guide
item.description: Inflation is a general, sustained rise in prices and a fall in the purchasing power of money. How it is measured (the consumer price index), its types and causes (demand, cost, money supply), the difference between nominal and real income, and how the central bank controls it. A facts-based, sourced guide, using data from the Central Bank of Uzbekistan and the IMF.

item.title: World Bank: Uzbekistan's Poverty Fell From 17% to 5.8%, Middle Class Roughly Doubled
item.description: 3.7 million people left poverty in 2021–2025; but most new jobs are informal and prosperity is uneven across regions.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Resume ATP and WTA Tennis Tournaments, Aiming for Asia's Top 5 by 2030
item.description: Under a presidential decree, ATP, WTA and ITF tournaments will be held regularly from October 1; costs will be covered by charitable donations.

item.title: How inheritance is distributed in Islamic law: the basics of fara'id
item.description: Inheritance (mirath) is a precisely defined branch of Islamic law, the science of fara'id. Which four things are taken from the estate and in what order, the fixed shares (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 2/3, 1/3, 1/6), why a son takes twice a daughter's share, and the shares of husband, wife, parents and children. A facts-based, sourced guide, based on the Qur'an (Surah An-Nisa) and the four schools of law.

item.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to Visit Samarkand in October With Over 100 Companies
item.description: Rubio will take part in a C5+1 ministerial; the visit was announced by US special envoy Sergio Gor.

item.title: Uzbekistan to revive international tennis: ATP and WTA return from October 1
item.description: A presidential decree of 21 September orders Uzbekistan to resume ATP, WTA and ITF tournaments. By 2030 the country aims for 3,000 regular players, 200 coaches and a place among Asia's top five tennis nations.

item.title: The Uzbek diaspora in Afghanistan: how it formed
item.description: Afghanistan is home to the world's largest Uzbek community after Uzbekistan itself: an estimated 3.7–6.1 million Uzbeks live in the north. How this community formed — a Turkic population over centuries, the fall of Bukhara in 1920, the migration of the Basmachi and collectivization eras, and the situation today. A facts-based, sourced history.

item.title: More Than 100 Delegates Walk Out of Netanyahu's UN General Assembly Speech
item.description: 24 September: the Israeli PM defended his positions on Gaza and Iran; the Palestinian president called it a genocidal war.

item.title: 'Enterprise Uzbekistan': English Law and Tax Breaks Through 2100 for Tech Firms
item.description: A separate legal regime based on English law, zero taxes and three-year visas is being offered to international technology companies.

item.title: The Bukharan émigrés: the Uzbek diaspora in Turkey and Saudi Arabia
item.description: The fall of the Emirate of Bukhara in 1920, the Basmachi movement and Soviet policy drove thousands of Central Asians into exile — via Afghanistan — to the Hijaz (Saudi Arabia) and Turkey. The formation of the "Turkistani"/"Bukhari" communities, with dates and sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Monitor Cotton Pickers' Working Conditions From 25 September
item.description: The Federation of Trade Unions will inspect farms with 65 specialists; figures on last year's violations were released.

item.title: Uzbekistan's national currency: the introduction of the som (1993–1994)
item.description: Leaving the ruble zone after independence, the introduction of the sum-coupon on 15 November 1993, and the launch of the national currency — the som — on 1 July 1994. With dates, figures and official sources: the history of a milestone of economic sovereignty.

item.title: Uzbekistan Beats India in Samarkand to Take Sole Lead at the Chess Olympiad
item.description: The team won all six of its matches; in round six it defeated defending champions India 2.5-1.5.

item.title: Uzbekistan citizenship and dual citizenship: the rules
item.description: Under the 2020 Law on Citizenship: Uzbekistan does not recognize dual citizenship; how citizenship is acquired; and what happens to someone who takes a foreign citizenship (it is not automatic). A practical, facts-based guide for the diaspora abroad.

item.title: Lithuania to Close Visa-Document Centers in Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The centers will stop operating on 1 November; the interior minister cited security risks and the threat of terrorism.

item.title: How zakat is calculated and to whom it is given: a full guide
item.description: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam. What the nisab is, which wealth the 2.5% applies to, to whom the money may be given — the eight categories — and the difference between zakat and zakat al-fitr. A facts-based, sourced guide, using the 2026 (1447 AH) figures of the Muslim Board of Uzbekistan as an example.

item.title: At the UN, Saida Mirziyoyeva Says Uzbekistan's Choice Is Human Dignity
item.description: The head of the Presidential Administration addressed the 81st UN General Assembly in Uzbek, citing figures from economic and social reforms.

item.title: Russian Diesel Returns, but Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan Remain Exposed
item.description: Russia sharply increased diesel supplies to Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan in August. Yet both import almost all their fuel and stay vulnerable to disruptions in Russia.

item.title: How the Hajj and Umrah are organized: quotas, queues and rules
item.description: The Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam. Its timing and rites, the Saudi quota system, global pilgrim numbers, and how Hajj and Umrah are registered from Uzbekistan — a facts-only guide.

item.title: YouTube Monetization in Uzbekistan: Saida Mirziyoyeva Discusses It With Google
item.description: Uzbekistan's Presidential Administration head met Google VP Karan Bhatia in New York to discuss launching monetization. Per CERR, Uzbekistan loses up to $50 million a year.

item.title: A U.S. Green Card and the paths to it: the DV lottery and more
item.description: The main routes to a Green Card (permanent residence) — family, employment, the Diversity Visa (DV) lottery and asylum — plus the rules for becoming a citizen and how to avoid fraud. Uzbekistan leads the world in DV selections. A facts-only guide.

item.title: France's Internal-Security Attaché for Central Asia Starts Work in Tashkent
item.description: Cyril Gou is France's only internal-security attaché in the region. His mandate covers five Central Asian states and areas from organised crime and cybercrime to migration.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva to Represent Uzbekistan at the 81st UN General Assembly
item.description: The head of Uzbekistan's Presidential Administration is taking part in the general debate in New York and met UN Secretary-General António Guterres.
